supplementals.Title: Sunburn
supplementals.Content_XHTML:
Treatment of Sunburn Pain

MedicationDosageNotes

Acetaminophen

  • Tylenol Regular Strength
  • Tylenol Extra-Strength
  • Tylenol Adult Liquid Pain Reliever

325 mg Regular Strength Tablets or Caplets

  • 650 mg (2 pills) every 4 to 6 hours

500 mg Extra Strength Gelcaps, Caplets, or Tablets

  • 1000 mg (2 pills) every 8 hours

500 mg Liquid per Tablespoon

  • 1000 mg (2 tablespoons or 30 cc) every 8 hours
  • For pain relief you can take acetaminophen.

Instructions for Taking Acetaminophen

  • Regular Strength Tylenol: Take 650 mg (two 325 mg pills) by mouth every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Each Regular Strength Tylenol pill has 325 mg of
  • acetaminophen.
  • Extra Strength Tylenol: Take 1,000 mg (two 500 mg pills) every 8 hours as needed. Each Extra Strength Tylenol pill has 500 mg of acetaminophen.
  • The most you should take each day is 3,000 mg.

Extra Notes and Warnings:

  • Acetaminophen is in many over-the-counter and prescription medicines. It might be in more than one medicine that you are taking. You need to be careful and not take an overdose. An acetaminophen overdose can hurt the liver.
  • Caution: Do not take acetaminophen if you have liver disease.
  • Before taking any medicine, read all the instructions on the package.

Ibuprofen

  • Advil
  • Motrin

200 mg Caplets or Tablets

  • 200 to 400 mg (1 to 2 pills) every 6 hours
  • For pain relief you can take ibuprofen.
  • Take 200 to 400 mg (1 to 2 pills) by mouth every 6 hours.
  • The most you should take each day is 1,200 mg (6 pills), unless your doctor has told you to take more.
  • Use the lowest amount that makes your pain feel better.

Extra Notes and Warnings:

  • Acetaminophen is thought to be safer than ibuprofen in people over 65 years old.
  • Caution: Do not take ibuprofen if you have stomach problems, kidney disease, are pregnant, or have been told by your doctor to avoid this type of anti-inflammatory drug.
  • Caution: Do not take ibuprofen for more than 7 days without consulting your doctor.
  • Before taking any medicine, read all the instructions on the package.

Preventing Sunburn

MedicationDosageNotes

Use a sunscreen with a SPF of 15 to 30. Broad-spectrum sunscreens (UVA and UVB protection) are best.

Sunscreens with ratings higher than 30 provide minimal additional protection.

Apply sunscreen to areas that can't be protected by clothing.

Generally, an adult needs about 1 oz of sunscreen lotion to cover the entire body.

Reapply every 2 to 4 hours and after swimming. You should also reapply after exercising or sweating.

  • Sunscreens help prevent sunburn but do not completely prevent skin damage. Thus, sun exposure can still increase your risk of skin aging and skin cancer.
  • Try to avoid all sun exposure between 10:00 am and 3:00 pm.
  • Also, use a hat with a wide brim and cotton clothing with long sleeves when outdoors.

  • Bacitracin ointment (OTC in U.S.) or
  • Polysporin ointment (OTC in Canada) or
  • One that you already have.

 

Put a small amount of antibiotic ointment on the wound. Cover it with an adhesive bandage (such as a Band-Aid) or a dressing. Change daily or if it becomes wet.

Apply ointment 2 to 3 times a day.

Caution: Stop ointment if a rash or allergic reaction occurs.

Liquid Skin Bandage

  • New Skin
  • Curad Spray Bandage
  • 3M Nexcare No Sting Liquid Bandage Spray

Use after cleaning the wound. Needs to be applied only once.

 

You can use an over-the-counter liquid skin bandage for minor cuts, scratches, and scrapes.

You can use this instead of using an antibiotic ointment and a regular bandage (e.g., gauze dressing or Band-Aid).

  • Caution: Do not take ibuprofen if you have stomach problems, kidney disease, are pregnant, or have been told by your doctor to avoid this type of anti-inflammatory drug.
  • Caution: Do not take ibuprofen for more than 7 days without consulting your doctor.
  • Before taking any medicine, read all the instructions on the package.

supplementals.Content_XHTML:
Poison Ivy, Oak, and Sumac

MedicationDosageNotes

Reducing the Itch of Poison Ivy with Calamine Lotion (Zinc Oxide)

  • Calamine Lotion

Apply to affected area of the skin 3 to 4 times daily.

 

 

Reducing the Itch of Poison Ivy with Hydrocortisone Cream

  • Hydrocortisone Cream 1%
Apply to affected area of the skin 3 to 4 times daily for 5 days.
  • Hydrocortisone is a low-strength steroid that can help provide relief for minor skin irritations like the rash from poison ivy, oak, or sumac.
  • Keep the cream in the refrigerator. It feels better if applied cold.

Extra Notes and Warnings:

  • Caution: Do not use hydrocortisone cream for more than 1 week without talking to your doctor.
  • Caution: Do not use if the cause is ringworm, impetigo, Jock Itch, or Athlete's Foot.

Reducing the Itch of Poison Ivy with an Oatmeal Bath

  • Aveeno (Oatmeal) Bath

 

Sprinkle contents of 1 packet under running faucet with comfortably warm water. Bathe for 15 to 20 minutes, 1 to 2 times daily.
  • After using Aveeno bath, pat the skin dry using a towel; do not rub.
  • You can also dry the area by using a blow dryer set on the cool setting.

Caution: The tub may be slippery after taking an oatmeal bath.

Treatment of Hives (Urticaria)

MedicationDosageNotes

Cetirizine

  • Zyrtec

 

10 mg Cetirizine Tablets

  • 10 mg every day

Cetirizine is a newer (second-generation) antihistamine and it causes less sedation than diphenhydramine. It has the added advantage of being long-acting (lasts up to 24 hours).

Caution:

  • Antihistamines may cause sleepiness.
  • Do not drink alcohol, drive, or operate dangerous machinery while taking antihistamines. 

 

Diphenhydramine

  • Benadryl

25 mg Diphenhydramine Tablets

  • 25 to 50 mg every 6 hours

Caution:

  • Antihistamines may cause sleepiness.
  • Do not drink alcohol, drive, or operate dangerous machinery while taking antihistamines. 

Fexofenadine

  • Allegra

Fexofenadine Tablets

  • In Canada, the adult dose is one 24-hour table (120 mg) once a day. Or, you can take on 12-hour (60 mg) tablet 2 times a day.
  • In the United States, the adult dose is one 24-hour tablet (180 mg) once a day.

 

Fexofenadine is a newer (second-generation) antihistamine and it causes less sedation than diphenhydramine. It has the added advantage of being longer-acting.

supplementals.Title: Smoking Cessation
supplementals.Content_XHTML:
Over-The-Counter Medications that Help with Smoking Cessation (Quitting Smoking)

MedicationDosageNotes

Nictotine Gum

  • Generic nicotine gum (drug stores may have their own brand)
  • Nicorette

 

People who smoke their first cigarette more than 30 minutes after getting up in the morning:

  • Use the 2-mg gum.
  • Chew the gum slowly until it begins to tingle in your mouth. Then put it between your cheek and teeth/gums. When the tingle is gone, begin chewing again. After about 30 minutes it will stop tingling.
  • Weeks 1 to 6: Chew 1 piece every 1 to 2 hours. This means that on average 10 to 16 pieces a day.
  • Weeks 7 to 9: Chew 1 piece every 2 to 4 hours.
  • Weeks 10 to 12: Chew 1 piece every 4 to 8 hours.
  • Consider stopping the gum when you are down to 1 to 2 pieces of gum a day.
  • Maximum dose: Do not use more than 24 pieces a day.
  • Read the package instructions on all medications you take.

Heavy smokers (more than 25 cigarettes per day) or people who smoke their first cigarette less than 30 minutes after getting up in the morning:

  • Use the 4-mg gum.
  • Chew the gum slowly until it begins to tingle in your mouth. Then put it between your cheek and teeth/gums. When the tingle is gone, begin chewing again. After about 30 minutes it will stop tingling.
  • Weeks 1 to 6: Chew 1 piece every 1 to 2 hours. This means that on average 10-16 pieces a day.
  • Weeks 7 to 9: Chew 1 piece every 2 to 4 hours.
  • Weeks 10 to 12: Chew 1 piece every 4 to 8 hours.
  • Consider stopping the gum when you are down to 1 to 2 pieces of gum a day.
  • Maximum dose: Do not use more than 24 pieces a day.
  • Read package instructions on all medications you take.
  • Do not eat or drink for 15 minutes prior to using nicotine gum.
  • Do not eat or drink while chewing nicotine gum. This can interfere with the effect of the gum.

Extra Notes and Warnings:

  • Side effects of the gum include mouth sores, dizziness, headache, and nausea. Some people can get jaw muscle pain from chewing. Tell your doctor if you think you are having side effects.
  • Caution: Do use nicotine gum and continue to smoke.
  • Caution: Do not chew more than one piece at a time.
  • Caution: Talk with your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
  • Caution: Talk with your doctor before using if you have any serious medical problems, including heart problems, thyroid problems, poorly controlled high blood pressure, or stomach ulcers. Talk with your doctor before using if you have jaw joint problems (TMJ syndrome).

Nicotine Lozenge

  • Generic nicotine lozenge (drug stores may have their own brand)
  • Nicorette

 

People who smoke their first cigarette more than 30 minutes after getting up in the morning:

  • Use the 2-mg lozenge.
  • Place the lozenge in your mouth. Let it slowly dissolve.
  • Weeks 1 to 6: Use 1 lozenge every 1 to 2 hours. This means that on average 10 to 16 pieces a day.
  • Weeks 7 to 9: Use 1 lozenge every 2 to 4 hours.
  • Weeks 10 to 12: Use 1 lozenge every 4 to 8 hours.
  • Consider stopping the lozenges when you are down to 1 to 2 lozenges a day.
  • Maximum dose: Do not use more than 1 lozenge an hour. Do not use more than 20 lozenges a day.
  • Read the package instructions on all medications you take.

Heavy smokers (more than 25 cigarettes per day) or people who smoke their first cigarette less than 30 minutes after getting up in the morning:

  • Use the 4-mg lozenge.
  • Place the lozenge in your mouth. Let it slowly dissolve.
  • Weeks 1 to 6: Use 1 lozenge every 1 to 2 hours. This means that on average 10 to 16 pieces a day.
  • Weeks 7 to 9: Use 1 lozenge every 2 to 4 hours.
  • Weeks 10 to 12: Use 1 lozenge every 4 to 8 hours.
  • Consider stopping the lozenges when you are down to 1 to 2 lozenges a day.
  • Maximum dose: Do not use more than 1 lozenge an hour. Do not use more than 20 lozenges a day.
  • Read the package instructions on all medications you take.
  • Do not eat or drink for 15 minute prior to using a nicotine lozenge.
  • Do not eat or drink while using a nicotine lozenge. This can interfere with the effect of the lozenge.

Extra Notes and Warnings:

  • Side effects of the lozenge include sore throat, mouth irritation, heartburn, dizziness, headache, and nausea. Tell your doctor if you think you are having side effects.
  • Caution: Do use nicotine lozenges and continue to smoke.
  • Caution: Do use more than one lozenge at a time.
  • Caution: Talk with your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
  • Caution: Talk with your doctor before using if you have any serious medical problems, including heart problems, thyroid problems, poorly controlled high blood pressure, or stomach ulcers.

 

Nicotine Patch

  • Generic nicotine patch (drug stores may have their own brand)
  • Nicoderm CQ

Smoke less than 10 cigarettes a day:

  • Place a new patch on at the beginning of each day. Put it on a new place on your body each day.
  • The goal is to step-by-step use lower dose patches.
  • Step 1: Use one 14 mg patch/day (weeks 1 to 6).
  • Step 2: Use one 7 mg patch/day (weeks 7 to 8).
  • Read the package instructions on all medications you take.

Smoke more than 10 cigarettes a day

  • Place a new patch on at the beginning of each day. Put it on a new place on your body each day.
  • The goal is to step-by-step use lower dose patches.
  • Step 1: Use one 21 mg patch/day (weeks 1 to 6).
  • Step 2: Use one 14 mg patch/day (weeks 7 to 8).
  • Step 3: Use one 7 mg patch/day (weeks 9 to 10).
  • Read the package instructions on all medications you take.
  • If you are having trouble sleeping at night, you may want to wear the patch for only 16 hours a day (take it off at night).
  • If you wake up in the morning craving a cigarette, then you may want to leave the patch on for 24 hours a day.

Extra Notes and Warnings:

  • Side effects of the patch include local skin irritation, dizziness, headache, difficulty sleeping, and nausea. Tell your doctor if you think you are having side effects.
  • Caution: Do use nicotine patches and continue to smoke.
  • Caution: Do use more than one patch at a time. Do not cut patches in half.
  • Caution: Talk with your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
  • Caution: Talk with your doctor before using if you have any serious medical problems, including heart problems, thyroid problems, poorly controlled high blood pressure, or stomach ulcers.

supplementals.Title: Index Report - Specialty Clinics
supplementals.Content_XHTML:
Best practice for telehealth triage nursing is to identify the primary reason for call (chief complaint) and to triage the symptom(s).

  • For most specialty practices, the majority of calls are symptom-related.
  • Even for specialty calls, focusing on the primary reason for call (symptoms such as abdomen pain, cough, chest pain) is usually the best place to start.

The index shown below lists just selected specialties and in many cases just the most relevant telehealth triage guidelines. See the Alphabetic Index for a complete list of all the symptom-based (211), injury (51), and other guidelines that can be used in a specialty clinic.

The 2024 update of the Adult After-Hours Telehealth Triage Guidelines consists of 434 active guidelines. There are 20 new guidelines and 414 updated prior active guidelines.
